_schema.about: Flowable Atlas project graph. Query it — do not read it whole; a large project runs to megabytes.
_schema.node: {id: '<type>:<key>', type, label, key, file, data, usedBy?}
_schema.absent: A key whose value would be null is not written, here and in every record below: `.file`, `.resultVariable` and the like answer null either way, so test a value, not `has(...)`.
_schema.dataIn: A model or changelog node's data lives once in the named top-level bucket — find it by matching type+key there (e.g. data.dataIn='processes' -> .processes[] | select(.key=="<key>"), data.dataIn='liquibase' -> .liquibase[] | select(.key=="<key>")).
_schema.java: javaByRole ({role: [class]}) and javaGlue list Java classes as {fqn, file, line}; what Atlas read from a class — roles, bean names, methods, endpoints — is on the node 'java:<fqn>' (a class Atlas gave no role, listed under 'other', mostly has none). Controllers are javaByRole.controller.
_schema.usedBy: Node ids that reference this node: the sources of its edges (app 'contains' membership excluded; the relation itself is in `edges`) and, for variable, expression, binding, string, serviceOperation and customFunction nodes, the models that use them (where and how: data.reads, data.writes, data.usages).
_schema.findings: {check, kind, severity, node, label, message, file?, element?, subject?, line?, scriptLine?, models?, snippet?, waived?} — what Atlas thinks is wrong. `kind` is 'defect' (wrong now) or 'advice' (worth a look), whatever the severity; `checks` counts the open ones per check plus a `waived` total. `subject` tells apart several findings of one check on one node (the scope, the column), where `message` is prose that rewords. `line` is a line of `file`: the element's declaration, the reference a missing model is named by, or the script line a script problem sits on; `scriptLine` is a line within the script body, given when no file line could be. `models` lists the models an expression or binding finding sits in. `waived` carries the reason a team accepted it; see `waivers` and waivers.json.
_schema.waivers: {rules: [{check, node, element?, subject?, reason, by?, at?, until?, matched}], createdWith?, notes?: [{node, check?, element?, subject?, text, importance, by?, at?}], stale?, unexplained?, problems?} — present when a waivers.json was read: what it covered, and what is wrong with the file.
_schema.modelCopies: {'<type>:<key>': {<file>: <fingerprint>}} — present when a model is held in more than one file (a Design export beside its -bar.zip): every file of it, with a fingerprint of what that copy says. The node and the bucket show the first copy only.
recipes: models using variable V:     jq '.graph.nodes[] | select(.id=="variable:V") | .usedBy'
controller serving a form:   jq '.restCalls[] | select(.source|test("X")) | .matches'
what we accepted, and why:   jq '.findings[] | select(.waived) | {check, label, reason: .waived.reason}'
